# Making your own site package

This section is for developers, designers, agencies and hosts who want new Exponential installations to start from
their own site: their own content classes, demo content, settings, roles and design, chosen in the setup wizard or
named in `kickstart.ini` like the 7x packages are. It answers: where to start, what you change, how the archives are
built, where they are published, and how an installation finds them.

7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage you to submit your site package by pull request to
[se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth](https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth):
an accepted package becomes available through the default distribution system, the setup wizard, the kickstarter and
ezupdate, on every installation. How to do that is on [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).

## The path in short

A site package is an ordinary Exponential package of type `site` whose `package.xml` names the packages it requires
and the PHP files the installer runs at fixed points of the `CreateSites` step
([What a site installer package is](../basics/what-a-site-installer-package-is.md)). Making your own one is mostly
copying a working one and changing it:

```text
fork a source repository      sevenx-ezpackage or cjw_multisite-ezpackage, packages/<name>/ per package
  -> rename and edit           package.xml, the installer script, the content classes and the demo content
  -> rebuild the archives      packages/build.sh: one <name>.ezpkg per package folder
  -> publish                   a static HTTPS folder with index.xml, the .ezpkg files and thumbnails/
  -> point an installation     package.ini [RepositorySettings] RemotePackagesIndexURL, kickstart.ini Site_package
  -> test in a sandbox         exp:install --dry-run, then a throwaway install
```

The 7x site packages were made exactly this way. `cjw_multisite`, published with release 6.0.15, is a fork of
`sevenx_multisite`: it keeps `sevenx_classes` as a requirement, brings its own demo content package
(`cjw_multisite_democontent`) and its own installer class (`cjwMultiSiteInstaller` in
`settings/cjw-multi-site-installer.php`), and lives in its own repository,
[se7enxweb/cjw_multisite-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/cjw_multisite-ezpackage), "laid out as the 7x package
repository" (its first commit, 7 October 2026).

## What you need before you start

- [ ] An Exponential 6.0 installation you can throw away (a separate checkout with SQLite is enough), never the
      production site: the installer writes the database and the settings.
- [ ] git and a GitHub account (or any git host) for the source repository of your packages.
- [ ] A shell with `tar` and `gzip`; `xmllint` helps to check XML files.
- [ ] For publishing: a place that serves static files over HTTPS (GitHub Pages works, as the 7x server shows).
- [ ] A license decision for the code, the documentation and the demo images
      ([Licensing choices](../../designers/distribution/licensing-choices-overview.md)).

> **Note**
> The installer reads site packages; it does not care how they were made. Everything in this section works the same
> whether you build the archives with `build.sh`, with `ezpm` or by hand, as long as each archive passes the checks
> of [Validating a package before publishing](../requirements/validating-a-package-before-publishing.md).

## Two ways to share the result

| Way | Who gets it | What you run |
|---|---|---|
| Pull request to the 7x package server | every installation, in its setup wizard, kickstarter and ezupdate, with no settings changed | your packages are reviewed and published with the next release folder ([Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md)) |
| Your own package server | installations whose `package.ini` points at your server, or that add it in ezupdate | a static HTTPS folder you keep up to date ([Running your own package server](running-your-own-package-server.md)) |

Both can be combined: test on your own server, then send the pull request.

> **Tip**
> Start from the requirements checklist ([The requirements checklist](../requirements/the-requirements-checklist.md))
> so the package is ready for review from its first version, and keep a changelog from the first commit.
